record.paper_title: Seven open problems in applied combinatorics
record.original_question: Let G=(V,E,ω) be a weighted simple graph. Construct an algorithm that computes an ε-net L⊂V for G and simultaneously improves on the existing ε-net algorithms by using fewer landmarks and running in less time than the currently available methods.

evidence.quote: Three different methods to obtain -nets in metric graphs, namely, the greedy, iterative and SPTpruning algorithms, are proposed in [1]. These algorithms are experimentally compared with respect to the number of landmarks they produce for the same graph, including their execution time.

Open Problem 1.2. For a weighted simple graph G = (V, E, ω), propose an algorithm to construct an -net for G such that: (i) It is based on a lower number of landmarks than that of the existing algorithms; (ii) The time of execution of the algorithm is lower than the existing algorithms.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E, ω) be a weighted simple connected graph with edge-weight function ω : E → ℝ_{>0}, inducing the shortest-path (geodesic) metric d_G on V. For ε > 0, a subset L ⊆ V is called an ε-net of G if:
(a) for every v ∈ V there exists ℓ ∈ L with d_G(v, ℓ) ≤ ε (covering), and
(b) for any two distinct ℓ, ℓ' ∈ L one has d_G(ℓ, ℓ') > ε (packing/separation).
Elements of L are called landmarks.

Three known procedures for constructing such an ε-net are:
(i) a greedy algorithm that repeatedly selects a vertex at distance > ε from the current set of landmarks;
(ii) an iterative algorithm that updates landmarks via local exchanges;
(iii) an SPT-pruning algorithm based on pruning shortest-path trees.

Design an algorithm A that, given any input (G, ε), outputs an ε-net L ⊆ V of G and simultaneously satisfies both of the following:
(1) The cardinality |L| produced by A is, in the worst case (and/or on benchmark instances on which the three algorithms above have been compared), strictly smaller than the cardinality produced by each of the greedy, iterative, and SPT-pruning algorithms.
(2) The running time of A is strictly smaller than that of each of the greedy, iterative, and SPT-pruning algorithms.

Equivalently: provide an ε-net construction that strictly improves both the landmark count and the running time of all previously known ε-net algorithms for weighted simple graphs, or prove that no such algorithm exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open problem in a 2023 list of seven open problems in applied combinatorics. A targeted web search did not surface any subsequent paper or preprint claiming an ε-net algorithm for weighted simple graphs that simultaneously beats the greedy, iterative, and SPT-pruning algorithms in both landmark count and running time. The status therefore appears to remain open.
